post.description: Marks the contact as rejected: it disappears from the review queue, is excluded from campaign scheduling (readyForCampaign is reset to false), and will not be picked up by automatic campaign launches. Providing a reason is optional but recommended: reasons are stored on the contact and help understand why leads are rejected so targeting can be refined. Calling this route on an already-rejected contact only updates the reason (latest reason wins); the original rejection timestamp and reviewer are kept. post.description:
Designed for first-party signals: actions a lead takes in your own product or stack, pushed programmatically the moment they happen. Hook it to any event you already track (a lead signs up for a free trial, books a demo, attends your webinar, downloads your pricing guide, upgrades to a paid plan...) and the signal is added to the contact, next to the signals detected by Gojiberry agents, most recent first. Anything that can send an HTTP request can feed it: your backend, a CRM workflow, a form or scheduling tool webhook, Zapier, Make or n8n. The possibilities are endless.

To send a first-party signal, describe what happened in intent (e.g. "Booked a demo from the pricing page"), optionally add a short label in intentKeyword (e.g. "demo_booked"), and leave intentType empty. Signals without an intentType are recorded on every call, so repeated events (a second demo, another webinar) are all kept; make sure your integration sends each event only once.

Set intentType only to record one of the signal types detected by Gojiberry agents. A typed signal the contact already has (same intentType and intentKeyword) is not recorded twice and the call returns created: false; HIRING, HIRING_SURGE, NEW_DECISION_MAKER, RECENT_ACTIVITY, RECENTLY_CHANGED_JOB and RECENT_FUNDING_EVENT are recorded at most once per contact, whatever the keyword. At least one of intent, intentType or intentKeyword is required.

post.description: Create a campaign with its steps, lead source lists and sending seats. A campaign is the **campaign agent** — the outreach half of a **Full Cycle agent**: create the list first (`POST /v1/list`), then the source agent that fills it with leads (`POST /v1/agent`), then this campaign to reach out to them. **At least one list (lead source) is required.** The campaign reaches out to the contacts of its lists; lists are typically filled by a source agent (the lead finder, see `POST /v1/agent`) or by importing contacts. If the campaign contains any LinkedIn step (invitation, invitationNote, message, voiceMessage, visitProfile, likePosts), a `linkedinSeatId` is required. If it contains email steps, at least one `emailSeatId` is required; multiple email seats (up to 100) are only allowed when the campaign has email steps exclusively. Step rules: at most one Connection Request step, an invitation cannot come after a LinkedIn message or voice message, and `delayAfterLastStep` must be at least 1 day (see the `steps` field for per-type fields and limits). When the campaign has a Connection Request step, 1st-degree connections are excluded from the campaign by default. **Once activated, the campaign starts the outreach automatically on a daily basis.** The launch hours can be configured in the LinkedIn seat settings.

Returns the actions queued for this campaign, as shown in the Scheduled tab of the app: one entry per contact with the step to run (invitation, invitationNote, message, voiceMessage, visitProfile, likePosts or email), its message filled with the contact variables, and the last step the contact already received. It sends nothing and does not pull new contacts into the campaign, generate AI messages, or look up emails, so no credit is spent. As on the campaign page, the planner still updates the contacts it reads: a contact with no step left is marked finished, a step it cannot perform (no email, unsubscribed, no LinkedIn profile) is marked skipped or the contact excluded, and a blocklisted company is flagged. post.description:
Create a new source agent (the lead finder) for the authenticated user. **A list is mandatory: the agent imports the leads it sources into a list, so you must create a list first (`POST /v1/list`) and link it to the agent through the required `listId` field.** If the active agent limit is reached, the agent is still created but paused. A source agent only finds leads — it does no outreach. Without a campaign agent attached to the same list, it shows up as a **legacy agent** in the platform. Best practice is to follow up with `POST /v1/campaign` using the same list as lead source, forming a **Full Cycle agent** (list + source agent + campaign agent) that sources and reaches out to leads automatically.

**Signals (`variables`)**: the agent finds leads through its signals. `variables` is optional, but when sent it must hold 4 to 15 signals, and an "autopilot" agent created without it is accepted but has nothing to run. Each signal is a `{ "type", "value" }` object, and **the `value` format depends on the `type`**: a quoted keyword of 1 to 3 words for `SEARCH_KEYWORD` (`"\"cold email\""`), a LinkedIn company page URL for `COMPETITOR_PAGE_URL` (`https://www.linkedin.com/company/lemlist`), a LinkedIn profile URL for `INFLUENCER_PAGE_URL` (`https://www.linkedin.com/in/johndoe`), the literal `"true"` for event signals (`RECENTLY_CHANGED_JOB`, `HIRING`, ...), and a lowercase technology name for `TECHNOLOGY` (`hubspot`). `VISITED_PROFILE` and `YOUR_COMPANY_FOLLOWERS` also need `needsUserToken: true` and a `linkedinSeatId`. The API does not validate values: a malformed keyword, URL, or technology is saved anyway, and that signal then finds no leads or the wrong ones. The `value` field of the variable schema lists the exact format for every type.

info.title: Gojiberry AI - External API
info.description:
# Gojiberry AI External API

This API allows you to programmatically access your Gojiberry AI data and integrate it with your applications.

## How it works

Gojiberry runs your outreach as a pipeline of three building blocks:

1. **Source agent — the lead finder.** A source agent continuously sources leads matching your targeting criteria (job titles, industries, locations, signals, ...) and scores them with AI.
2. **List — where the leads land.** Every source agent is linked to a list (`listId` is required when creating an agent): the leads it finds are imported as contacts into that list. Lists can also be filled by importing contacts yourself.
3. **Campaign — the outreach.** A campaign uses one or more lists as its lead source (`listIds` is required when creating a campaign) and runs its steps (LinkedIn invitations, messages, emails, ...) on the contacts of those lists, sending through your LinkedIn and/or email seats. Once activated, the campaign runs the outreach automatically on a daily basis.

**Terminology.** In the Gojiberry platform, an **Agent** is a *campaign agent* — the campaign that performs the outreach. A **source agent** is the lead finder that sources the leads. The two are linked through a **list**: the source agent imports the leads it finds into the list, and the campaign agent reaches out to the contacts of that list.

**Best practice: create a Full Cycle agent.** Always create the three resources in this order — first the list, then the source agent that fills it, then the campaign that reaches out to it. Together, the list + source agent + campaign agent form a **Full Cycle agent**: leads are sourced and outreached automatically, end to end. If you create a source agent without a campaign agent, it shows up as a **legacy agent** in the platform: it only sources leads and does **no outreach**. So it's best practice to always create all three.

A typical setup through the API:

```text
POST /v1/list                  # 1. create the list
POST /v1/agent                 # 2. create the source agent (lead finder) linked to that list (listId)
POST /v1/campaign              # 3. create the campaign agent using that list as lead source (listIds)
GET  /v1/campaign/{id}/logs    # 4. follow the outreach activity
```

## Authentication

All API requests require authentication using a Bearer token. To get your API key:

1. **Log in to your Gojiberry AI account** at [https://app.gojiberry.ai](https://app.gojiberry.ai)
2. **Navigate to Settings** → **API** section
3. **Click "Create API Key"** to generate a new token
4. **Copy the API key** when it's displayed (you won't be able to see it again)
5. **Use the token** in your requests by adding the header: `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY`

## Impersonation (organization owners)

If your API key belongs to the **owner of an organization**, you can perform any API call on behalf of another member of your organization by adding the `x-impersonate-user-id` header with the member's user ID:

```bash
# Get the contacts of the organization member with user ID 123
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
     -H "x-impersonate-user-id: 123" \
     https://ext.gojiberry.ai/v1/contact
```

When impersonating, the request behaves exactly as if it was made by that member: you read and write their data (contacts, campaigns, lists, unibox, etc.).

Rules:
- Your API key must belong to the **organization owner**; other members cannot impersonate.
- The impersonated user must belong to the **same organization** as the API key user.
- Requests that don't meet these rules are rejected with a `401 Unauthorized`.

Tip: use `GET /v1/organization/members` to list the members of your organization and their user IDs, and `GET /v1/user/me` to verify which user the current request acts as.

## Rate Limits

- **100 requests per minute** per account. Short bursts above this are tolerated.
- **100,000 requests per day** per account.
- Limits are shared by all API keys and AI app (MCP) connections of the same user, including calls made on behalf of organization members with `x-impersonate-user-id`.
- Requests over a limit return `429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header (in seconds). Wait that long before retrying.
- Some endpoints have their own lower limit, stated in their description.

## Base URL
- **Production**: `https://ext.gojiberry.ai`

## Endpoints

### Contacts
- `GET /v1/contact` - Get all contacts with filtering and pagination
- `GET /v1/contact/{id}` - Get a specific contact
- `GET /v1/contact/health` - Health check endpoint

## Example Usage

```bash
# Get all contacts
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
     https://ext.gojiberry.ai/v1/contact

# Get contacts with filtering
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
     "https://ext.gojiberry.ai/v1/contact?search=john&agent=1&dateFrom=2024-01-01"

# Get a specific contact
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY" \
     https://ext.gojiberry.ai/v1/contact/123
```

## Webhooks

Gojiberry allows you to receive real-time notifications when new contacts are created or updated by configuring a webhook URL.

### How to Configure Webhooks

1. **Log in to your Gojiberry AI account** at [https://app.gojiberry.ai](https://app.gojiberry.ai)
2. **Navigate to the Integrations page** at [https://app.gojiberry.ai/integrations](https://app.gojiberry.ai/integrations)
3. **Add a Webhook integration** by clicking the Webhook option
4. **Enter your webhook URL** where you want to receive notifications
5. **Save the configuration**

Once configured, Gojiberry will send POST requests to your webhook URL whenever:
- A new contact is created
- A contact is updated
- Other relevant events occur in your account

The webhook payload will include the full contact data in JSON format. Each webhook request includes a custom header `x-gojiberry-user-id` containing your user ID for verification purposes.

### Verifying Webhook Signatures (optional)

You can optionally configure a signing secret on your Webhook integration. When a secret is set, every webhook request also includes:

- `x-gojiberry-timestamp`: the Unix timestamp (in seconds) at which the request was sent
- `x-gojiberry-signature`: `sha256=` followed by the hex-encoded HMAC-SHA256 of `{timestamp}.{rawBody}` computed with your signing secret

To verify a request:

1. Read the raw request body as a string (do not re-serialize parsed JSON).
2. Concatenate the value of `x-gojiberry-timestamp`, a `.` character, and the raw body.
3. Compute the HMAC-SHA256 of that string using your signing secret, hex-encoded, and prefix it with `sha256=`.
4. Compare it to `x-gojiberry-signature` using a constant-time comparison.
5. Reject requests whose timestamp is too old (we recommend a 5 minute tolerance) to prevent replay attacks.

Example in Node.js:

```js
const crypto = require('crypto');

function verifyGojiberrySignature(rawBody, headers, secret) {
  const timestamp = headers['x-gojiberry-timestamp'];
  const signature = headers['x-gojiberry-signature'];
  if (!timestamp || !signature) return false;
  if (Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(timestamp)) > 300) return false;
  const expected = 'sha256=' + crypto.createHmac('sha256', secret).update(timestamp + '.' + rawBody).digest('hex');
  return expected.length === signature.length && crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(expected), Buffer.from(signature));
}
```

If no signing secret is configured, these headers are not sent.

## Support

For API support, please contact us at [hello@gojiberry.ai](mailto:hello@gojiberry.ai)

deepResearchEndedAt.description: When the latest deep research ended for this contact

customFields.description: Custom fields imported from CSV, keyed by normalized snake_case name (rendered with the custom_ prefix)

campaignStatus.description: Campaign status information. Useful to know what is the achieved step of the contact in the campaign — i.e. how far the contact has progressed through the campaign's sequence. The stepNumber matches the campaign's step numbers (the steps defined on the campaign), so a stepNumber of 2 means the contact has reached step 2 of that campaign.

signals.description: Every signal recorded for the contact, most recent first (agents and LinkedIn pools)

userId.description: User ID who owns this contact

content.description: Message content for this campaign step

parts.description: Derived conversation parts when split is enabled

subject.description: Email subject for this campaign step. Only used when the step is an email step. When editing an email step, always resend the subject together with the content — even if only the content changed — otherwise the stored subject is erased.

stepNumber.description: Campaign step number this message applies to. Please refer to the campaign.steps array !

stepId.description: Server-managed stable id of the campaign step. Read-only: the server derives it from stepNumber on write, any sent value is ignored. Declared so stored messages can be resent as-is.

audioUrl.description: Server-managed audio of an AI voice message step, spoken in the account’s cloned voice. Read-only: generated voice messages are kept as stored and any sent value is ignored. Declared so stored messages can be resent as-is.

aiVoiceId.description: Server-managed id of the cloned voice that spoke `audioUrl`. Read-only: any sent value is ignored. Declared so stored messages can be resent as-is.

intent.description: Intent or activity description for the contact

readyForCampaign.description: Mainly used for review mode campaigns: setting this to true accepts the lead for the scheduled queue, so it is picked up at the next campaign launch without manual review. Also set by the AI agent when a contact should be scheduled.

state.description: Contact state. Set to "paused" to stop a contact from progressing in the campaign. Send null to clear the state. Possible values: "paused" (stops campaign progression), "finished" (completed all steps), "1stnetwork" (1st degree LinkedIn connection), "excluded" (excluded from all campaigns), "answered" (replied to a message).

personalizedMessages.description: Personalized messages for each campaign step. This array REPLACES the stored messages: always resend every step you want to keep, with all of its fields (content, subject, parts). Any step or field left out of the payload is erased.

intent.description: Human-readable description of what the lead did, as it should appear on the contact
intent.example: Booked a demo from the pricing page

intentType.description: Leave empty for first-party signals. Only set it to record one of the signal types detected by Gojiberry agents.

intentKeyword.description: Short label for the signal, e.g. trial_signup, demo_booked or webinar_attended

steps.description: Campaign steps, executed in order. Valid types: invitation, invitationNote, message, voiceMessage, visitProfile, likePosts, email. Ordering rules: at most one Connection Request step (invitation or invitationNote); an invitation cannot come after a message or voiceMessage step. Common fields: delayAfterLastStep in days (integer >= 1, default 2). stepNumber is assigned automatically from the array order and unknown fields are ignored. message and email steps take a messageMode: 'ai' (content is generated by AI for each contact, the default when no content is provided) or 'same' (the provided content is sent as-is, supports the [FirstName], [LastName], [Company], [JobTitle], [SenderFirstName], [SenderName], [SenderFullName] and [SenderCompany] variables; an empty value removes the tag). In 'same' mode, message is required (max 1900 chars for LinkedIn messages) and email steps also require subject. invitationNote requires note (max 180 chars, 280 with a Sales Navigator seat); voiceMessage requires url to the audio file; likePosts accepts numberOfPosts (1-3, default 1); visitProfile and invitation need no extra fields.

listIds.description: IDs of the lists used as lead source. At least one list is required.

linkedinSeatId.description: LinkedIn seat sending the LinkedIn steps. Required when the campaign contains any LinkedIn step; not allowed on email-only campaigns.

emailSeatIds.description: Email seats sending the email steps. Required when the campaign contains email steps. Multiple seats (up to 100) are only allowed on email-only campaigns. Use GET /v1/email-seat to list your email seats and their IDs.

active.description: Whether the campaign starts active. Once active, the campaign starts the outreach automatically on a daily basis; the launch hours can be configured in the LinkedIn seat settings.

listIds.description: List IDs to associate with the campaign

steps.description: Campaign steps. Must have the same length and step type order as the existing campaign; only message and messageMode are updated.

active.description: `true` to activate the campaign, `false` to deactivate it

campaignId.description: Campaign ID associated with this list

type.description: Type of signal: what the agent looks for. It sets the expected format of `value` (see `value`).

value.description:
Value of the signal. Its format depends on `type`. **The API does not validate it: a malformed keyword, URL, or technology is saved anyway, and that signal then finds no leads or the wrong ones.** Use one item per variable (one keyword, one URL, one technology), as the Gojiberry app does.

**Keyword signals**: people who liked or commented on recent LinkedIn posts containing the keyword.
- `SEARCH_KEYWORD`: one keyword of 1 to 3 words, wrapped in double quotes so LinkedIn matches the exact phrase. The value is the string `"cold email"` including its quotes (`"\"cold email\""` in JSON). This is the keyword type the Gojiberry app creates.
- `SEARCH_KEYWORD_COMMENT` (commenters only), `SEARCH_KEYWORD_LIKE` (likers only), `SEARCH_KEYWORD_POST` (post authors): same value format. Legacy types not offered in the app; prefer `SEARCH_KEYWORD`.

**LinkedIn page signals**: people who liked or commented on the recent posts of a LinkedIn page. The value is the page URL, never a website URL or a name. Remove sub-paths and query strings (`/about/`, `/posts/`, `?...`).
- `COMPETITOR_PAGE_URL`: a company page (competitor, partner, or your own company): `https://www.linkedin.com/company/<slug>`, e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/company/lemlist`. `/school/` pages also work; `/showcase/` pages are not supported.
- `INFLUENCER_PAGE_URL`: a person (expert or creator in your market): `https://www.linkedin.com/in/<slug>`, e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/in/johndoe`.
- `YOUR_PROFILE`: your own LinkedIn profile: `https://www.linkedin.com/in/<slug>`.
- `YOUR_COMPANY`: legacy. Use `COMPETITOR_PAGE_URL` with your own company page instead.

**Signals run on the user's own LinkedIn account**: also set `needsUserToken: true` and `linkedinSeatId`.
- `VISITED_PROFILE`: people who viewed the profile of the LinkedIn account behind `linkedinSeatId`. That account needs LinkedIn Premium or Sales Navigator. Value: `"true"`.
- `YOUR_COMPANY_FOLLOWERS`: followers of your LinkedIn company page. The account behind `linkedinSeatId` must be an admin of the page. Value: the page URL with its numeric company ID (the ID in the page admin URL), `https://www.linkedin.com/company/<numeric id>`, e.g. `https://www.linkedin.com/company/107433042`.

**Event signals**: the value is ignored, always send `"true"`. Never put a funding round, job title, or description in it (e.g. "Series A", "hiring SDRs"). Leads come from the agent targeting (`targetJobTitles`, `targetIndustries`, `targetLocations`, `targetCompanySizes`). Each event signal runs at most once every 72 hours.
- `RECENT_ACTIVITY`: people matching the targeting who are active on LinkedIn.
- `RECENTLY_CHANGED_JOB`: people matching the targeting who recently started a new job.
- `NEW_DECISION_MAKER`: people who recently started a Director-level or higher role. `options: { "seniority": "vpPlus" }` narrows it to VP level and above.
- `RECENT_FUNDING_EVENT`: people at companies that recently raised funds.
- `HIRING`: people at companies that are hiring.
- `HIRING_SURGE`: people at companies whose hiring is growing fast.

**Tech stack signal**
- `TECHNOLOGY`: people matching `targetJobTitles` (required for this signal) at companies that use a technology. Value: one technology slug, which is the lowercase technology name with its spaces and punctuation kept, e.g. `hubspot`, `salesforce`, `google analytics`, `amazon aws`, `asp.net`. Matching is exact (case-insensitive), so a variant spelling such as `google-analytics` or `Google Analytics 4` finds nothing. Same values as `technologiesUsed` in `POST /v1/directory/companies/search`.

**Not usable in `variables`**
- `LOOKALIKE`: refused. Create the agent with `agentType: "lookalike"` instead.
- `WEBSITE_VISITOR`: create the agent with `agentType: "website-visitor"` instead of adding it here.
- `JOB_SEARCH`: refused for now.
- `EVENT_KEYWORD`, `GROUP_KEYWORD`: accepted but never run, so they never find leads.

options.description: Type-specific settings. Through the API, only `NEW_DECISION_MAKER` reads one: `{ "seniority": "vpPlus" }` keeps VP-level and higher roles only (default: Director-level and higher). Omit it for every other type.

enabled.description: Whether the signal runs. Defaults to true. Set to false to keep the signal on the agent without running it.

needsUserToken.description: Set to true for `VISITED_PROFILE` and `YOUR_COMPANY_FOLLOWERS` only, together with `linkedinSeatId`: these signals must run on the user's own connected LinkedIn account. Leave it unset for every other type.

linkedinSeatId.description: ID of the user's connected LinkedIn seat that runs the signal (the same seat ID as a campaign's `linkedinSeatId`). Required for `VISITED_PROFILE` and `YOUR_COMPANY_FOLLOWERS`, with `needsUserToken: true`. Leave it unset for every other type.

listId.description: ID of the list the agent imports its sourced leads into. A list is mandatory: create one first (POST /v1/list) and pass its ID here. The list must belong to the authenticated user.

targetJobTitles.description: Target job titles to search for

variables.description: The signals the agent tracks to find leads. Each variable is one signal: one keyword, one LinkedIn URL, one event, or one technology. Send between 4 and 15 variables. An "autopilot" agent created without variables has no signal to run. Optional for "website-visitor" agents (the website visitor signal is added automatically) and not allowed for "lookalike" agents. Each variable needs a `type` and a `value` whose format depends on the type. See `value` for every type: quoted keyword, LinkedIn page URL, `"true"` for event signals, or lowercase technology name. **Values are not validated: a malformed keyword, URL, or technology is saved anyway, and that signal then finds no leads or the wrong ones.** LOOKALIKE variables are refused, and JOB_SEARCH variables are refused for now.

ignoredCompanies.description: Companies to ignore in search results

mandatoryKeywords.description: Keywords that must be present in the profile

leadWaterfall.description: Enable smart lead finder mode, usually true

paused.description: Create the agent paused. Note: the agent is also created paused when the active agent limit is reached.

minLeadScore.description: Minimum lead score threshold (0–1) - Usually 0.6 or 0.8

maxCreditUsage.description: Max number of credits per month (website visitor agent only)

id.description: Unique identifier of the agent log entry.

leadsCreated.description: Number of leads imported into the user platform after the AI scoring & filtering pipeline. These are the qualified leads that ended up on the agent's list and become contacts of the linked outreach campaign.

totalLeads.description: Total number of raw leads the agent found from this signal in this run, BEFORE any AI scoring or filtering. Always greater than or equal to leadsCreated.

errorMessage.description: Error message if the run failed for this signal. Null when the run succeeded.

agentType.description: Type of signal the agent ran (e.g. SEARCH_KEYWORD, COMPETITOR_PAGE_URL, RECENT_FUNDING_EVENT). Matches the agent's configured signal types.

agentKeyword.description: The specific signal value used in this run — e.g. the keyword searched, the competitor page URL watched, or the lookalike seed. Lets you see which signal produced which leads.

agentId.description: ID of the agent this log entry belongs to.

createdAt.description: When this log entry was recorded (ISO 8601).

targetJobTitles.description: Target job titles to search for

agentType.description: Type of agent, only "autopilot" is accepted

variables.description: The agent's signals. **Replaces the whole list**: send every signal to keep, not only new or changed ones. Between 4 and 15 variables, with the same per-type `value` formats as `POST /v1/agent`. LOOKALIKE and JOB_SEARCH variables are refused.

ignoredCompanies.description: Companies to ignore in search results

mandatoryKeywords.description: Keywords that must be present in the profile

listId.description: ID of the list to associate with this agent

scriptInstalled.description: Whether the visitor tracking script is installed on the website (website-visitor agents)

maxCreditUsage.description: Max number of credits per month

lastMessage.description: Content of the last message in the thread

lastMessageDate.description: Date of the last message in the thread

lastMessageFullName.description: Full name of the sender of the last message

seen.description: Whether the thread has been seen

attendeeUrn.description: LinkedIn URN of the attendee (conversation partner)

attendeeProfilePicture.description: Profile picture URL of the attendee

seatId.description: LinkedIn seat id owning the thread

interested.description: Sentiment: whether the attendee is interested

aiGeneratedReply.description: AI-generated draft reply for the operator to review

contactId.description: Linked Gojiberry contact id, when matched

createdAt.description: When the thread row was created

updatedAt.description: When the thread row was last updated

data.description: Threads on this page, ordered by last message date

total.description: Number of threads matching the filters

page.description: Page that was requested. Starts at 1.

totalPages.description: Number of pages for this filter

id.description: Attachment id, used by the download endpoint

seatId.description: LinkedIn seat id that received/sent the message

linkedinMessageBackendUrn.description: LinkedIn's message backend URN (urn:li:messagingMessage:…). Used with user/thread scoping as the dedup key when the same message arrives via both the realtime SSE stream and the getThread backfill.

senderIsSelf.description: True when the sender is the seat owner

deliveredAt.description: Timestamp LinkedIn assigned when the message was delivered (voyager `deliveredAt`). Distinct from `createdAt`, which is when the row landed in Gojiberry — for backfilled history those can differ by years.

createdAt.description: Timestamp the row was persisted in Gojiberry

total.description: Number of messages in the thread

page.description: Page that was requested. Starts at 1.

totalPages.description: Number of pages in the thread
